（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C.I.D. REGISTRY No. 6412 Date February 26, 1929）

Further REPORT

Subject (in full) British Lady reported missing.

Made by D. S. Widdowson, Forwarded by [Signature]

On February 26th, 1929, Mrs Hudson telephoned the under-
signed, and was later interviewed by appointment at St. Faith's
Settlement, No. 50/2 Jessfield Road, a School kept by Miss M.
Henderson.

Mrs. Hudson states that she has left her husband for good,
owing to his cruelty to her before Chinese, and as she lives in
fear of him, she does not wish to divulge her address. She states
that she is going to communicate with H. B. M. Consular Authorit-
ies immediately, as Mr. Hudson has control of her money, and
passport etc. Communication may always be established with her
through Miss Henderson, but she begs that this information be
kept from her husband.

[Signature]

Shanghai Municipal Police.

Central Station.

February 20th, 1929.

Further REPORT ON British Lady reported missing.

Made by D. S. Widdowson, Forwarded by Aubrey Cr.

On February 20th, 1929, Mr. Hudson informed me that his wife was on very friendly terms with a Miss Burdick, of the Seventh Day Adventist Mission, Pont St Catherine. The lady was interviewed and gave the following information:- Mrs Hudson visited her on February 18th and told her that she had left her husband, rather than work at his office as he had demanded. She stated that she was living by herself in rooms, and refused to divulge her address, and that she intended to remain away from her husband until he agreed to change his views regarding her work at his office, and gave an undertaking to cease his over-bearing conduct. ( The latter failing appears to have been noticed by many of the lady's friends, who sympathise with her. ). Mrs. Hudson was in good health and perfectly normal at the time. Complainant has been informed, and under the circumstances, I beg to suggest that no further Police action is necessary, as it is apparent that nothing untoward has happened to the lady.

（批：Yes, but we could keep in touch and see how the matter develops. W.H.）

Mr Hudson informed of above.

D. S. Widdowson.
Senior Det. ( C ).

Supt. " B " Division.

关于英籍女士报失踪的补充报告。

制作人：D. S. 威多森，转呈人：奥布里 Cr.

1929年2月20日，哈德森先生告知我，他的妻子与庞圣凯瑟琳（Pont St Catherine）基督复临安息日会传教团的伯迪克小姐关系非常友好。对该女士进行了面谈，她提供了以下信息：哈德森夫人于2月18日拜访了她，并告诉她，自己已离开丈夫，而不愿像丈夫要求的那样在他的办公室工作。她称自己独自居住在房间内，拒绝透露住址，并表示打算一直远离丈夫，直到他同意改变对她在其办公室工作的看法，并承诺停止其专横的行为。（后一种失败的表现似乎已被该女士的许多朋友注意到，他们都同情她。）哈德森夫人当时健康状况良好，精神完全正常。投诉人已获知上述情况，鉴于此情形，谨建议无需警方采取进一步行动，因为显然该女士并未遭遇不测。

（批：是的，但我们可以保持联系，看看事态如何发展。W.H.）

已将上述情况告知哈德森先生。

D. S. 威多森。
高级探员 ( C )。

“B”分区警司。

下属 13。
用于结合之前的报告。
并放入 C。
作为流转档案。
情况表明无需采取进一步行动。
我发现该女士精神完全正常。
她告诉我，她离开丈夫是因为他想让她在他的办公室工作，而她拒绝了。
她正与朋友住在一起，不希望别人知道她的地址。
当他同意让她随心所欲时，她会回来。
未怀疑有不法行为。
结案。

Shanghai Municipal Police
Central Station.

February 19th, 1929.

REPORT ON British Lady reported missing.

Made by D. S. Widdowson, Forwarded by Conway C.

At 6-40 p.m., February 18th a telephone message was received from Hongkew Station to the effect that a Mr. Hudson, of No. 2 Museum Road reported his wife missing since February 12th. Attempts were made in vain to get in touch with complainant at that address on the same date, but details as supplied by Hongkew were circulated.

When interviewed at his office, The Commercial Exchange, No. 62 Kiangse Road, Mr. Hudson gave the following details:- On February 9th he went to Ningpo on business, leaving his wife at No. 2 Museum Road, where the couple live in a room over a book-shop. Complainant asked his wife to attend his office on February 12th and 13th when he would be absent. On his return on February 14th complainant learnt that his wife had not been seen since February 12th and had not been to his office. No effort was made to trace her until February 18th, as complainant says he thought she may have gone to visit some of her various Missionary friends, of whom she has many, both in Shanghai, and up country. Subsequently Hospitals etc have been visited by complainant, and his wife is not there. After making a report to Hongkew, complainant discovered that his wife had sent a letter, dated February 18th, 1929; to some Chinese pupils at the home of Dr. Chang, Gordon Road, stating that she would discontinue her lessons and appoint a substitute. Complainant seems to have no fears for his wife's safety, and apparently was in bed when detectives tried to interrogate him on February 18th. Mrs. Hudson apparently has undertaken to supply a friend in U. S. A. with a quantity of Chinese pictures on a commission basis, and seems to have left home to carry out this

关于英籍女士报失踪的报告。

制作人：D. S. 威多森，转呈人：康韦 C.

2月18日下午6时40分，接到虹口捕房的电话留言，称博物馆路2号的哈德森先生报告其妻子自2月12日起失踪。同日试图在该地址联系投诉人未果，但已分发虹口捕房提供的详情。

在江西路62号商业交易所（The Commercial Exchange）其办公室接受面谈时，哈德森先生提供了以下细节：2月9日他因公务前往宁波，将妻子留在博物馆路2号，夫妇二人住在一家书店楼上的房间里。投诉人要求妻子在他缺席的2月12日和13日到他的办公室去。2月14日回来后，投诉人得知自2月12日以来无人见过他的妻子，且她未去过他的办公室。直到2月18日才努力寻找她，因为投诉人称他认为她可能去拜访她在上海及内地众多的传教士朋友中的某几位。随后投诉人走访了医院等处，但其妻不在那里。向虹口捕房报案后，投诉人发现其妻曾寄出一封日期为1929年2月18日的信，给戈登路张医生家中的一些中国学生，声明她将停止授课并指派一名替代者。投诉人似乎并不担心妻子的安全，且2月18日侦探试图讯问时他 apparently 还在床上。哈德森夫人显然承诺以佣金为基础向美国的一位朋友供应一批中国画，似乎离家是为了执行此

（批：什么时间？
下午1点。下午1点半。
以及晚上9点。
1929年2月18日。）

Made by D. S. Widdowson, Forwarded by Aubrey Cl.

On March 1st, 1929, Mr. Martin, H. B. M. Consular Magistrate
was interviewed re Mrs. Hudson. He states that the lady has
already stated her case to him, and efforts are being made to
obtain a separate passport for her to enable her to leave Shanghai,
as she no longer wishes to live with her husband. We have been unable to
interview Mr. Hudson so far, but he will be referred to H. B. M.
Consulate for further information when seen.
